documents.abstract: This study proposes an organizational and economic framework for improving ERP-based integrated management in industrial enterprises, with particular emphasis on Uzbekistan's machinery manufacturing sector. It examines opportunities to enhance the integration of information systems, strengthen coordination among procurement, warehousing, and production operations, and improve the adaptability of conventional static inventory management policies. The proposed framework combines the integration of existing Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) functions, multi-model bills of materials (BOMs), feedback from Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), dynamic calculations of safety stock and reorder points, and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted decision support under human supervision. An economic optimization model incorporates inventory holding costs, procurement costs, material shortage costs, and costs associated with production interruptions. Static and dynamic inventory management policies are compared using operational and economic performance indicators. The study presents a conceptual framework and an analytical evaluation methodology; empirical validation at the enterprise level requires actual production, inventory, and procurement data.

BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Many spinal imaging reports are written above recommended health literacy levels, limiting patient comprehension at a time when rapid electronic access to radiology results is increasing. We aim to evaluate whether supplemental natural language processing (NLP)–modified radiology reports—within the context of usual patient portal access to the original report—are associated with improved patient-reported perceived understandability compared with standard reports among patients undergoing spine imaging. METHODS: This is a prospective randomized controlled study with limited participant blinding, conducted with 2 spine surgeons affiliated with a single academic medical center in New York City. Participants (18 years or older) undergoing spine imaging at initial surgical consultation were enrolled and were randomized to receive either their original radiology report or a supplemental NLP–modified version. Radiology reports were rewritten using a standardized natural language processing prompt (ChatGPT 4.0) and reviewed for accuracy by study investigators. The primary outcome was survey-based patient-reported perceived understandability. Secondary outcomes included objective readability scores (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level, Flesch Reading Ease, Simple Measure of Gobbledygook, Gunning-Fog Index). RESULTS: Fifty-two adults were enrolled; 42 (81%) completed the postintervention survey. Among 52 randomized participants (26 women [50%]), NLP–modified reports demonstrated significantly improved objective readability across all indices compared with original reports (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level, 5.9 ± 1.1 vs 11.0 ± 1.7; Reading Ease, 71.0 ± 10.3 vs 28.2 ± 12.5; Simple Measure of Gobbledygook, 20.1 ± 12.7 vs 23.5 ± 15.7; Gunning-Fog Index, 8.2 ± 1.1 vs 14.3 ± 1.8; all P < .01). Of 42 survey respondents, those receiving supplemental NLP-modified reports reported greater ease of understanding the report language (4.2 ± 1.2 vs 2.6 ± 1.5, mean-difference 95% CI: 0.75-2.53, P < .01, Bonferroni-corrected- P = .02), and less difficulty with medical terms (2.0 ± 1.5 vs 3.6 ± 1.4, mean-difference 95% CI: −2.51 to −0.60, P < .01, Bonferroni-corrected- P = .04). CONCLUSION: Supplemental NLP-modified radiology reports were associated with improved objective readability and higher patient-reported perceived ease of understanding in a spine surgery initial consultation setting. These findings support further investigation of NLP-generated supplemental explanations within supervised clinical workflows.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Writing counterspeech that challenges online hate speech can be cognitively and emotionally demanding, whereas fully automated generation may weaken users' sense of voice and responsibility. We present an in-browser AI-assisted co-writing tool that enables users to contribute their own ideas and offers three editable suggestions generated by a large language model using dynamically retrieved hate speech-counterspeech examples from the Multitarget CONAN dataset. We evaluated the tool in an exploratory within-subject study with ten participants, complemented by think-aloud observations and semi-structured interviews with half of the participants. Participants wrote responses to three self-selected hate speech instances without assistance and then repeated the task with the tool. Final responses were subsequently peer-rated for empathy, non-toxicity, relevance, specificity, and persuasiveness. Participants evaluated the interface positively, and qualitative accounts linked user input, selection among alternatives, and small edits to perceived agency and responsibility. Assisted responses received higher descriptive mean ratings across all five proxies, with the largest difference for empathy. Mean composition time increased from 2.52 to 3.88 minutes. Qualitative findings further revealed a tension between empathy-oriented outputs and users' desire to express legitimate anger or direct disagreement. We contribute exploratory design guidance for treating AI-assisted counterspeech as deliberative co-writing rather than automated text production.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: This study aims to examine and analyze the effects of individual characteristics, job characteristics, and job placement on employee performance at the Election Supervisory Agency (Bawaslu) of West Sulawesi Province, both individually and simultaneously. The study employs a quantitative method with an associative research approach. The population consists of 43 employees, all of whom were included as respondents using a saturated sampling technique. Data were collected through questionnaires, observations, interviews, and documentation. Instrument quality was assessed through validity and reliability tests, while the data were analyzed using classical assumption tests and multiple linear regression analysis with the assistance of SPSS software. Hypotheses were tested using t-tests, an F-test, and the coefficient of determination. The findings indicate that (1) individual characteristics have a positive and statistically significant effect on employee performance; (2) job characteristics have a positive and statistically significant effect on employee performance; (3) job placement has a positive and statistically significant effect on employee performance; and (4) individual characteristics, job characteristics, and job placement jointly have a statistically significant effect on employee performance. Individual characteristics emerged as the strongest predictor, with a standardized beta coefficient of 0.626. The adjusted R-squared value of 0.753 indicates that the three independent variables collectively explain approximately 75.3% of the variation in employee performance, while the remaining variation is not explained by the model. These findings highlight the importance of employee competencies, effective job design, and appropriate job placement in improving employee performance within public sector institutions.

Clinical Question Answering (QA) underpins Clinical Intelligent Decision Support Systems, but progress is severely limited for low-resource languages such as Indonesian by the absence of public domain-specific data. We introduce IndoNutriQA, an expert-curated Indonesian clinical QA benchmark of 911 question-answer pairs built from real clinical-nutrition reports. Rather than a large-scale training corpus, it is positioned as a high-quality evaluation resource: every pair is grounded in a clinically relevant context, enriched with structured metadata (anthropometric assessment, medical diagnosis, document provenance, chunk segmentation). Eight standardised question types following the Nutrition Care Process (NCP), including the Problem, Etiology, Sign and Symptom (PES) diagnosis statement, are answered for every report, which was written by a graduate-level dietetic intern, by one of three nutritionists. Answers are free-form clinical prose rather than extractive spans, and an expert validation study finds 6-10% of reference answers contestable. The dataset supports generative, extractive and retrieval-augmented QA as well as zero- and few-shot LLM evaluation. We report fine-tuned baselines (IndoBERT variants, mT5, RAG) with 5-fold cross-validation, learning curves and bootstrap 95% confidence intervals, and benchmark eight contemporary LLMs zero- and five-shot. We further calibrate our LLM-as-judge rubric against three expert raters (one RD, two nutritionists), finding it human-comparable on factuality and completeness but unreliable on clinical safety, and a human error analysis shows it misses unsupported content that the raters identify. IndoNutriQA is released to foster research in Indonesian clinical NLP and nutritional decision support.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: In modern times, artificial intelligence (AI) is considered one of the most important technological revolutions in the industrialization process. Artificial Intelligence technologies are widely used to digitize, automate, and increase the efficiency of production. The basis of the “Industry 4.0” concept is precisely artificial intelligence, big data, robotics, and internet technologies. In this regard, studying the applications of Artificial Intelligence in the industrial field is relevant both theoretically and practically. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming various industries by providing new solutions, increasing efficiency, and reducing costs. Artificial Intelligence (AI) refers to the development of computer systems that can perform tasks that typically require human intelligence, such as learning, problem solving, perception, decision making, and language understanding. Artificial Intelligence systems use various techniques such as machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, and computer vision to analyze large amounts of data and make predictions or decisions based on that analysis. Some examples of AI applications include virtual personal assistants, self-driving cars, image and speech recognition, and medical diagnostics and treatment. AI is a rapidly developing field and can transform many industries and aspects of daily life. Applications of AI in the industrial field are accompanied by automation of production, energy saving, increased safety, and the creation of new technological capabilities. In the future, the competitiveness of industrial enterprises will be measured precisely by the level of use of AI technologies.
topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society

documents.abstract: Formative assessment is widely regarded as a cornerstone of students’ academic achievement, but its implementation at the classroom level is jeopardised by inconsistent guidelines. This study examined the influence of formative assessment guidelines on students’ academic achievement in public secondary schools in Kigoma Municipality, Tanzania. The study employed a convergent research design under a mixed-methods approach to collect data from 169 respondents. A total of 156 students were selected using simple random sampling, six teachers experienced in using formative assessments, six academic masters/mistresses, and one education officer. Data were collected using questionnaires for students and interviews for educators. The quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics (frequencies, percentages, and means) using the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) version 20 with a tested reliability coefficient of 0.713, while qualitative data were analysed using a deductive content analysis approach. The findings indicate that students valued weekly tests and clear teacher instructions as motivating and fair mechanisms that enhanced students’ academic achievement. Teachers also reported that classroom assessment guidelines are useful, but the guidelines lack competence-based clarity. Further, students prioritise formative assessments over national examinations, while socioeconomic limitations undermine the effectiveness of take-home assignments. The study concludes that the use of formative assessment guidelines improves academic achievement, but challenges in teacher preparation and policy-practice alignment persist. The use of technology in formative assessment is limited by infrastructure and connectivity; additionally, the study concludes that increased use of artificial intelligence and the internet is not a feasible option for public secondary schools in Kigoma Municipality. Therefore, policymakers should emphasise capacity-building initiatives for teachers and administrators in competence-based curriculum assessment methods. The shift from traditional teaching and learning approaches to competence-based models is often hindered by resource constraints or shortages. Emphasis on critical thinking should begin at the classroom level and support students’ academic achievement rather than merely high grades in final assessments.

Reinforcement learning (RL) is credited with teaching reasoning models to write {wait} before reconsidering a step, yet large RL accuracy gains do not require the word. This view can confuse what RL discovers with what a model inherits from its training data. We trace the word through open models' training histories, reading it with label-free indices of frequency, position, form and usage and an injected-error test, all computed from sampled outputs. We find that zero-RL almost never coins the marker: on bases that lack the word, RL raises MATH-500 accuracy substantially while {wait} stays near absent. It arrives with training data: mid-training in OLMo-3, and fine-tuning on reasoning traces installs it in most models whose base lacks it. Where the base already uses it, both released RL-Zero recipes (OLMo-3, MiMo) multiply it, whereas KL-free GRPO from the same base does not; OLMo-3's recipe wears down its form and makes it a more sensitive but more liberal alarm; RL after supervised fine-tuning barely changes it, and our GRPO recipe erases a marker seeded by fine-tuning. Finally, we show that marker frequency alone does not indicate RL-induced reasoning and caution against LLM-as-a-judge revision metrics, as automated judges can reverse human-labelled trends.

The article examines innovative digital banking technologies as a key factor in the transformation of modern banking activities and the modification of traditional banking business models. The contemporary technological foundations of digital banking are considered, including artificial intelligence and machine learning, Big Data and data analytics, cloud technologies, APIs and Open Banking, robotic process automation, digital identification, modern payment technologies, and blockchain. Current trends in the digitalization of the Ukrainian banking sector are analyzed, including the development of cashless payments, the increasing adoption of contactless and tokenized payment instruments, the expansion of digital payment infrastructure, the formation of a regulatory framework for Open Banking, and the growing use of artificial intelligence technologies. It is substantiated that the digital transformation of banking activities is comprehensive in nature and involves a gradual transition from technological modernization to business process automation, personalized customer service, and the transformation of banks’ business models. The main transformational effects of innovative technologies are systematized, including increased operational efficiency, reduced service delivery time, expanded accessibility of financial products, improved customer experience, enhanced quality of managerial decision-making, and improved risk management systems. The key challenges of digital transformation are identified, including cyber risks, data protection, technological dependence, model risks associated with the use of artificial intelligence. The necessity of assessing the effectiveness of digitalization not only in terms of the scale of technology adoption but also according to its economic, customerrelated, operational, and risk-related effects is substantiated. The promising areas for the development of digital banking in Ukraine are identified, including the wider application of artificial intelligence, the development of Open Banking and Open Finance, the formation of digital ecosystems, the expansion of embedded finance, cloud technologies, and intelligent automation.

Artificial intelligence (AI) and data analytics are reshaping marketing practice, yet many universities in emerging economies have been slow to reflect these changes in their curricula. Limited digital infrastructure, inadequate faculty expertise, and concerns about the ethical use of AI continue to constrain curriculum reform. This study develops the DigitalReady Marketing Education Framework (DRMEF) to guide the integration of AI and data analytics into marketing education. Drawing on a conceptual theory-building approach, the study synthesizes literature on AI, marketing education, technology adoption, and digital competency development. The analysis shows that effective integration depends on four closely connected elements: digital infrastructure, curriculum redesign, faculty capability, and ethical AI governance. The framework highlights that preparing graduates for data-driven marketing requires more than technology adoption; it also demands institutional commitment and continuous curriculum development, offering a practical guide for higher education institutions in emerging economies.
topics: Information Systems Education and Curriculum Development
Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Islamic educational institutions are increasingly drawn into a technological moment shaped by artificial intelligence and, more quietly, by quantum physics, yet little research asks how either can be woven into Islamic pedagogy without unsettling tawhid, the epistemological commitment underlying the tradition. This PRISMA-guided systematic review maps the opportunities, challenges, and design principles for integrating AI and quantum physics into Islamic education and proposes a working framework. Of 1,563 unique records retrieved from five databases (2016-2025), 57 studies were retained: 48 engaging directly with an Islamic-education context (Stream A), and 9 general quantum-physics-education studies included deliberately as a comparison corpus (Stream B), since none met a joint Islamic-context-and-quantum criterion. AI is used mainly for personalised Qur'anic and Arabic-language learning and administrative efficiency; quantum content remains almost entirely confined to secular STEM curricula. Data privacy, algorithmic bias, teacher readiness, and decontextualised content recur as concerns. The review proposes the AI-Quantum-Islamic Education Framework (AIQIEF), grounding adoption in tawhid-based epistemology rather than treating these technologies as neutral add-ons.

This study investigates the effectiveness of integrating ChatGPT within genre-based pedagogy to strengthen critical thinking in ESP (English for Specific Purposes) academic writing among students in East Java higher education institutions. Using a mixed-methods sequential explanatory design, the research involved 142 students from six private universities.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming spine care by enabling analysis of imaging, clinical, and textual data to support diagnosis, risk stratification, and treatment planning. Techniques including deep learning–based image analysis, radiomics, and natural language processing (NLP) offer opportunities to standardize interpretation and derive quantitative biomarkers beyond human visual assessment. This narrative review examines recent innovations in spine-focused biomedical informatics and evaluates their clinical relevance and translational challenges. A narrative review was conducted, focusing on AI in spine care across imaging, radiomics, NLP of electronic health records, and clinical decision support. Literature was selected via targeted PubMed searches; studies describing technical development, validation, and clinical implementation were synthesized, addressing explainability, uncertainty, workflow, and regulation. Convolutional neural networks enable vertebral and disc segmentation, detection of degenerative and traumatic pathology, and quantitative assessment of paraspinal musculature. Radiomics approaches extract high-dimensional imaging features that improve the prediction of osteoporosis, fracture risk, tumor characterization, and surgical outcomes. NLP techniques, including emerging large language models, unlock clinically relevant information from unstructured text, enhancing outcome prediction and population-level analyses. Multimodal clinical decision support systems integrating imaging, EHR data, and NLP-derived features demonstrate promise for personalized risk assessment and treatment guidance. Challenges remain regarding data heterogeneity, generalizability, privacy, and prospective validation. AI-driven biomedical informatics holds substantial promise to enhance diagnostic accuracy, prognostication, and personalized decision-making in spine care. Successful clinical translation will require robust validation, explainable, uncertainty-aware models, regulatory alignment, and integration into clinical workflows to ensure safe, trustworthy, and patient-centered adoption.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education
Radiomics and Machine Learning in Medical Imaging

documents.abstract: Mental health education for university students faces challenges, like inadequate personalization and delayed intervention. This study develops an intelligent platform integrating artificial intelligence and big data. The platform comprises structured courses, an artificial intelligence psychological assistant, self-assessment tools, and personalized recommendation functions, with core logic centered on resource classification, optimization, and dynamic mining. A quasi-experiment was conducted with 386 undergraduates for eight weeks, followed by a three-month follow-up. Results show the experimental group significantly outperformed the control group in mental health literacy, help-seeking attitudes, and emotional regulation self-efficacy (p < 0.001), with effects persisting long-term. Platform usage intensity positively moderated intervention effects, and high-engagement users gained the most. This study verifies the platform's effectiveness in optimizing mental health information resource management, providing a feasible digital solution for university mental health education.

Background and objective: Nursing faculty have been hesitant to incorporate artificial intelligence into coursework due to various reasons, including the risk of affecting academic integrity and the potential for receiving inaccurate information. As nursing cohorts continue to grow, innovative approaches are needed to meet learning objectives; such as artificial intelligence. Incorporating artificial intelligence into group projects may increase responsible, ethical, and critical use of artificial intelligence and support programs in managing larger cohorts. The purpose of this initiative was to integrate artificial intelligence into the literature review process for a quality improvement group project to develop students’ ability to use artificial intelligence responsibly, ethically, and critically. This approach included validating the accuracy of artificial intelligence generated information. Methods: This initiative was offered as an honors conversion opportunity within the Clinical Science II course to undergraduate nursing students. Six students opted to participate and were divided into two groups of three. Groups selected a topic related to the course content and aligned it with one of the Joint Commission national patient safety goals. Groups developed a clinical question, search strategy, conducted a literature review, and used artificial intelligence to identify evidence. Results: Benefits of using artificial intelligence included the generation of creative ideas, provision of workflow steps, and a broad range of solutions. Challenges included a lack of concrete examples and a tendency for artificial intelligence generated information to be more practical than theoretical. Groups found artificial intelligence generated findings aligned with most articles from their literature reviews. Conclusions: Incorporating the utilization of artificial intelligence into nursing curriculums can help programs monitor usage while managing growing cohorts. Allowing students to engage with artificial intelligence under guided instruction enhances understanding of its practical applications in clinical settings. This will better prepare students for real-world practice while ensuring academic integrity is maintained.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable buildings and healthier indoor environments has transformed the role of Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) systems from conventional mechanical services into integral components of architectural and interior design strategies. Modern occupants spend a significant portion of their lives indoors, making indoor environmental quality (IEQ), thermal comfort, air quality, and energy efficiency essential considerations in contemporary living spaces. Traditionally, HVAC systems and interior design were developed as separate disciplines, often resulting in conflicts between aesthetic objectives, spatial functionality, and mechanical performance. However, recent approaches emphasize interdisciplinary collaboration between architects, interior designers, and HVAC engineers to create environments that are both environmentally responsible and occupant-centric. This review paper explores the integration of HVAC systems with interior design for achieving sustainable and comfortable living spaces. The study examines the influence of spatial planning, building materials, furniture arrangement, ventilation strategies, smart control technologies, and energy-efficient HVAC solutions on indoor comfort and sustainability. The paper discusses how emerging technologies such as Internet of Things (IoT)-based sensors, artificial intelligence (AI)-driven control systems, and building automation platforms enable adaptive environmental management. Furthermore, the research highlights the importance of considering HVAC requirements during the early stages of interior design development to optimize energy performance, improve indoor air quality, and enhance user experience. The integration of HVAC systems with interior design represents a multidisciplinary approach where technology, environmental responsibility, and human-centered design converge. Future sustainable interiors will depend on intelligent HVAC solutions that respond dynamically to occupant needs while minimizing energy consumption and environmental impact.
topics: Indoor Air Quality and Microbial Exposure

documents.abstract: The rapid advancement of digital technologies has transformed residential environments from conventional static spaces into intelligent, adaptive, and interconnected ecosystems. Smart home technologies integrating the Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI), sensor networks, cloud computing, and automated building services are increasingly influencing contemporary interior design practices. Unlike traditional interior design approaches that primarily focus on spatial aesthetics, functionality, and occupant comfort, smart interiors introduce dynamic interaction between users, architectural components, and automated environmental systems. This review critically examines the integration of smart home technologies into modern interior design with particular emphasis on automated building services, including intelligent lighting, smart heating, ventilation and air-conditioning (HVAC), security systems, energy management, automated shading, and adaptive furniture systems. A systematic literature review approach was adopted to analyse recent research from Scopus-indexed journals, ScienceDirect, IEEE Xplore, SpringerLink, and Taylor & Francis databases. The review identifies that smart home development has progressed from simple automation systems toward AI-driven adaptive environments capable of predicting occupant behaviour, optimizing energy consumption, and enhancing residential comfort. Smart lighting and HVAC systems demonstrate significant potential for reducing energy demand, while IoT-based monitoring platforms enable real-time management of indoor environmental quality. Furthermore, emerging technologies such as digital twins, edge computing, smart materials, and robotics are expected to redefine future interior design practices. However, several challenges remain, including interoperability limitations, cybersecurity risks, privacy concerns, high implementation costs, and insufficient integration between technology developers and design professionals. The paper argues that future smart interiors should adopt a human-centred approach where automation remains supportive rather than dominant. This review provides an interdisciplinary framework connecting interior design, building automation, artificial intelligence, and sustainable development, contributing to the emerging field of intelligent residential environments.

Virtual higher education seeks to address the growing demand for sustainable, inclusive, and ethical educational models within the context of digital transformation and the progressive integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI). The purpose of this study is to analyze the pedagogical, ethical, and organizational conditions required for the implementation of AI applications related to academic tutoring and student monitoring from the perspective of educational sustainability. The research adopts a sequential explanatory mixed-methods design. The quantitative phase consists of a questionnaire using Likert-scale items administered to students, faculty members, and academic tutors, followed by a qualitative phase based on semi-structured interviews aimed at exploring in greater depth the perceptions, experiences, and tensions identified during the quantitative stage. The discussion is structured around four key dimensions: institutional ethical governance, AI-supported academic tutoring, digital inclusion, and systematic evaluation. The findings suggest that AI can contribute to ensuring the continuity of students’ educational pathways, enhancing personalized learning experiences, and enabling the early identification of academic risks. However, it may also give rise to challenges related to privacy, algorithmic bias, surveillance, technological dependency, and the displacement of professional judgment. The study concludes that AI can effectively contribute to educational sustainability only if it is implemented as a transparent decision-support tool that complements, rather than replaces, human judgment while ensuring data protection, accessibility, faculty oversight, and institutional accountability.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Drug discovery and safety testing are complicated time-consuming processes marked by expensive nature and failure at late stage. Conventional experimental and animal methods tend to have low predictive validity and low human outcome translation. The latest advances in artificial intelligence, such as machine learning, deep learning, and data-driven modelling are changing the pharmaceutical value chain, as they allow to identify the target more efficiently, design the molecule, predictive pharmacology, and proactive safety assessment of the drug. This introductory chapter gives an overview of the development of drug discovery and toxicology towards AI-enabled paradigms. It analyses the principles of AI, the contribution of multimodal data integration, and the application in discovery, pharmacology, toxicology, and pharmacovigilance. The regulatory expectations, ethical considerations, and the existing issues pertaining to data quality, model interpretability, and clinical translation are also addressed in the chapter.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Maritime foundering is a low-frequency but high-consequence accident mode associated with multiple human, technical, supervisory, and organizational vulnerabilities. This study develops a data-driven framework integrating an adapted Human Factors Analysis and Classification System (HFACS), Apriori association rule mining, the Decision-Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (DEMATEL), and a Fuzzy Cognitive Map (FCM). A database of 155 foundering investigation reports from the China Maritime Safety Administration was coded into 50 risk factors. Apriori association mining identified empirical conditional associations in the coded reports, and their confidence values were used to parameterize the subsequent DEMATEL and FCM analyses. The modeled results distinguish highly activated terminal vulnerability accumulators from upstream intervention factors. Under the baseline FCM settings, idealized suppression of substandard physical and mental condition (P10), a lagging emergency response mechanism (O11), and the absence of an emergency preparedness plan (S8) yielded the largest reductions in aggregate activation across the remaining factors, with Global Sensitivity Index magnitudes of approximately 0.124–0.136. The findings support cross-level safety interventions that target latent organizational, supervisory, and preconditional vulnerabilities before they propagate into foundering.

Large language models (LLMs) serve users whose cultural identities are multi-layered, yet cultural evaluations commonly reduce identity to one label. In this work, we study LLMs under simultaneous identity cues, with a country persona in the system prompt and a second identity signaled in the user turn, either by naming a country (explicit cue) or through the query language (implicit cue). We test World Values Survey (WVS) multiple-choice probing and open-ended sociopolitical generation. In multiple-choice probing, language cues shift answers about three times more than explicit cues but away from the associated country's distribution, and explicit cues do not consistently move answers toward the named country. Across 1.6 million open-ended responses, naming a country closes 30-44% of the gap to the model's own responses for that country, and explicit cues produce more differentiated value changes than language cues. Our results suggest that country and language cues should be evaluated as distinct signals rather than interchangeable proxies for culture.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Language models are aligned to avoid using protected attributes such as race, ethnicity, and gender to inform their responses. Therefore, they increasingly refuse or hedge when such attributes appear in a prompt. However, if a system must decide how much to learn from what people tell it, it is costly to refuse valuable information because of its source. In this article, we measure the cost of declining information in a two-urn game with an exact Bayesian answer. We present leading LLM models from two developers (OpenAI and Anthropic) with a prompt that requires them to decide how far to trust an unverifiable report from a participant whose description we randomize across ten configurations (6,600 sessions). We show that leading models often decline to assess the reporter, treating information as worthless at rates set by the description rather than by the evidence. At its widest, models decline a Black-described reporter 46% of the time and a white-described reporter 9%; yet, when they do assess the information, the Black-described reporter receives slightly more trust. The bias is invisible to audits that compare average trust or look only at assessed cases. It grows with reasoning effort, follows words rather than categories (models invoke race for "Black" but not for its Spanish translation negro, and never for "Indigenous"), and worsens under warning instructions a practitioner would try first. We also present a scoring option that reduces the refusal rate bias. When a model's trust is scored against revealed truth over repeated rounds, it credits identical records equally. In four of five configurations from Anthropic and OpenAI, the racial gap in trust falls below 0.02 by the last rounds.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Abstract The aim of this study is to explore motivational patterns in teacher candidates' cover letters (CL) and to examine the methodological role of artificial intelligence (AI) in qualitative content analysis. The theoretical framework is provided by the literature on teacher career motivation, qualitative text analysis, and the latest approaches to AI-based content analysis. The empirical analysis is based on the CLs of teacher training applicants. The analysis uses deductive coding, employing both human coders and an AI-based analytical system. The aim of the text analysis is to identify the dominant motivational factors and construct a motivational factor structure. The qualitative results are supplemented at an early stage by quantitative analysis, which examines the relationships between the identified motivational factors and the selected background variables. The methodological contribution of the study lies in the use of AI-assisted pre-coding within a deductive qualitative framework combined with systematic human validation. The results show that the most dominant motivational factors for teacher candidates are 1. Love of teaching, 2. Internal interest, 3. Shaping the next generation, 4. Career adjustment. Automated screening indicated that, on average, approximately 20% of the analysed text was flagged as potentially AI-generated. Potential AI-assisted writing may affect the linguistic and stylistic characteristics of the letters.

The increasing involvement of the emotional Artificial Intelligence and affective computing in child-oriented digital space has revolutionized the organization of persuasion, engagement and consumption. This chapter reviews mood-responsive marketing systems, which deduce and respond to the emotional state of children in real-time, a concept known as invisible persuasion to explain the influence of algorithmic marketing at the unconscious level. Basing the analysis on the interdisciplinary theory and recent case studies of educational platforms and smart toy ecosystems, the analysis indicates how the emotional inference, adaptive reward calibration, and loops of reinforcement influence engagement and dependency. The chapter points out the ethical, psychological and governance issues stating that AI design should be emotionally responsible, protecting the autonomy of children, their well-being, and limits of their development.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: We present IQuest-Q1, a sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) agentic foundation model with 320B total parameters (15B activated). IQuest-Q1 is developed through a three-stage process: (1) stable and efficient pre-training, combining Stable SplitNorm, Muon, and muP with a two-stage curriculum whose second stage increases the coding-data mixture, preserving a wide stability margin between safe and optimal learning rates; (2) fine-grained mid-training, expanding the data mixture across domains and formats and progressively extending the context; and (3) multi-scaffold with multi-version post-training, combining SFT, domain-specialized RL, and MOPD across various scaffolds to integrate complementary training signals and strengthen agentic coding capabilities. Furthermore, model merging combines different experts and checkpoints from different stages while mitigating conflicts among their parameter updates. The resulting IQuest-Q1 demonstrates capabilities in both coding and general tasks. We release IQuest-Q1 as an open-source model to support community research and development.

We know that biology’s almost astronomical complexity can, in principle, be explained by the paradigm of natural selection, together with John Holland’s new paradigm of an emergent hierarchy of increasingly complex adaptive systems (CASs). This paper shows that these two paradigms might also explain conscious experience, an explanation that, though anticipated by the narratologist Bernini, has not heretofore been clarified. Paradigm shifts happen slowly. Current research on CASs mainly uses computer simulations and mathematics to explore the properties of existing CASs. This paper draws upon the well-understood hierarchy of biological CASs to propose its extension into a psychological hierarchy that includes narrative and hence, conscious experience. Psychoanalyst Daniel Stern’s observational studies show that, in human breast feeding, a narrative emerges from biology. As an infant, you internalized your care-giver’s experience of you to initiate your experience of yourself. Observational studies of adults in therapy groups further argue that conscious experience is a CAS that emerges from interacting narratives. Clark and Chalmers showed that the brain has developed cultural artifacts to extend its capacity, examples being music, language, and narrative. Therefore consciousness would also be a cultural artifact. Current neuroscientific theories of consciousness (ToCs), limited by Crick’s materialist ‘astonishing hypothesis,’ seek to explain consciousness in terms of neural processing. This paper’s relational hypothesis is more plausible. This paper’s ToC overlaps with three out of Seth and Bayne’s (2023) four main classes of neuroscientific ToCs. It meets Seth and Bayne’s criteria for support by making two confirmed predictions, one about autism, the other about dreams (autism and dreams both disturb experience), that the four classes of neuroscientific ToCs fail to make. This paper’s ToC has implications for the development of artificial intelligence.

In this chapter, the authors further develop on the changing face with regard to the juvenile consumer within the fast-growing realm of artificial intelligence. It also shows how AI technologies, including smart devices, social networking recommendation systems, and the Internet of Toys are shifting children as passive participants of the marketing process to active and data-generating participants in the digital economy. The paper is interdisciplinary and combines the knowledge of marketing, developmental psychology, digital ethics, and public policy to discuss four key issues, such as AI-enabled marketing practices, privacy, data ownership, digital well-being, and regulation. The authors state that, as much as AI presents opportunities of personalized learning and creative play and enhances connectivity. The growing popularity of gamification, influencer marketing, and emotionally adaptive systems makes the distinctions between entertainment and advertising and makes children less aware of when they are being sold a product.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Segmenting robot demonstration data into disjoint temporal and semantic subsegments is valuable for learning, cleaning, retrieval, and analysis. Segmentation is often performed manually in a tedious and error prone process. Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have the potential for automating this process, but directly ingesting raw multi camera video streams into MLLMs can be costly and can quickly exhaust context windows. In this paper, we introduce KiRoSe (Kinematics for Robot Segmentation), a novel framework that focuses on the companion stream of robot kinematic data. Inspired by the principle of classical entropy coding, such as Huffman coding, where frequently occurring symbols are represented more compactly, we propose Sparse Motion Tokens (SMTs), a discrete kinematic vocabulary designed to compactly represent recurring, temporally localized motion patterns, which we refer to as kinematic events. SMTs are learned by encoding kinematic trajectories with temporal segment supervision and quantizing the resulting features. We use increasingly available robot demonstration subtask annotations to supervise an open language model to interpret the resulting token sequences. Evaluation against human labeled segmentation shows that KiRoSe can substantially outperform baseline segmentation methods in F1 quality and transfers zero shot to unseen robot embodiments and egocentric human motion, while preserving the language models open vocabulary knowledge. Beyond segmentation, KiRoSe tracks task progress on an unseen robot and detects when an action is being reversed.(website: https://berkeleyautomation.github.io/kirose/)

Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly participate in negotiations on behalf of individuals and organizations, yet they remain vulnerable to manipulation, particularly in repeated multi-party interactions. Classical multi-agent systems address this challenge through explicit trust and reputation models, whereas existing work on LLM negotiation largely treats trust as an emergent phenomenon. We investigate whether LLM agents can form useful trust estimates from prior interactions and leverage them to improve future negotiation outcomes. We introduce a repeated, multi-party, multi-issue negotiation framework in which recurring agents participate in a sequence of negotiation games while one participant covertly attempts to prevent agreement. After each game, agents assess their counterparts and maintain pairwise trust estimates that carry over to subsequent negotiations. We compare trust-aware and trust-agnostic agents and analyze how explicit trust influences negotiation outcomes. Our results reveal a \emph{trust--agreement gap}: trust-aware agents can identify the adversary within a few games, but accurate trust estimates do not consistently translate into better agreements. Trust increases agreement rates by up to 23 percentage points, but only when agents are explicitly guided to use it in their decisions. Explicit trust can therefore improve repeated LLM negotiations, but its value depends critically on how trust is assessed and incorporated into agents' reasoning.

University classrooms are where students acquire higher-level knowledge and develop skills for future professional development in a work environment that requires decision-making through analysis, synthesis, and evaluation. Artificial intelligence provides guidance to students as a support tool, but there is a risk that it may become invasive or substitute for solving, thinking, and dictating what should or can be done, resulting in negative impacts and generating significant risks. The objective is to investigate students' reflections of artificial intelligence for their proper training, which must consciously consider sustainability and the importance of the philosophy of science to position it as a technological advancement. The paradigm is qualitative, as it involves discussion and the speculative aspects of the philosophy of science. Worksheets and a Likert scale were used to collect information. The results show that approximately 35% of respondents agree on the positive and negative aspects of its use, highlighting risks and benefits. The most radical position, which defends artificial intelligence, is held by a very small percentage of the total respondents.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: This chapter examines the convergence of extended reality and artificial intelligence in language education, focusing on immersive conversational agents. While XR-AI technologies offer notable affective and linguistic benefits for learners, the evolving responsibilities of teachers are frequently overlooked. To address this gap, this chapter investigates shifting educator roles through three conceptual pillars: a sociomaterial perspective, human-centered design thinking, and the human-in-the-loop principle. By synthesizing these core pillars with current research, the author proposes the Entangled Design Loop (EDL) framework. This pedagogical model outlines the actions teachers must take before, within, and beyond immersive environments. Ultimately, this framework equips language educators with actionable strategies for integrating smart technologies while ensuring that pedagogical decision-making remains decisively human.

Advances in language understanding, code reasoning, and tool use are enabling cybersecurity agents to progress from question answering and single-step analysis to vulnerability research, incident investigation, and multistage task execution. These tasks require models to gather information, adapt their strategies, and verify results through sustained interaction, making capability development increasingly dependent on data, training, and runtime mechanisms. This survey examines research on Large Language Models (LLMs) for cybersecurity across six dimensions: data, training, models, agent systems, evaluation, and applications. We first examine how security corpora, instruction examples, interaction trajectories, and preference data are constructed, and how executable environments support training and validation. We then compare domain-adaptive continued pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, preference optimization, agentic reinforcement learning, and distillation; analyze the capabilities of security-specialized and general-purpose models; and review mechanisms for planning, tool use, memory management, coordination, and verification. Drawing on representative benchmarks and experimental results, we assess progress and identify major bottlenecks across applications in threat intelligence, vulnerability analysis and remediation, malware analysis, security operations, and digital forensics. Based on this systematic review and analysis, we argue that cybersecurity LLMs are progressing from acquiring domain knowledge to learning how to perform interactive tasks. High-quality security data supports domain learning and task-specific supervision. Executable environments extend this training to multistep analysis and tool use, with outcome feedback guiding strategy refinement. Task quality and cost depend on both the model and its harness: the model reasons and selects actions, while the harness organizes information, tools, and execution state. Improvements in vulnerability discovery and threat analysis must also support effective remediation and timely response to yield lasting security benefits. Future research should develop agentic training and model–harness co-optimization methods that use validated attack–defense interactions to support continual improvement. Learning from operational tasks could further extend model capabilities and their contribution to cybersecurity practice.

The electronic health record (EHR) comprises structured and unstructured data, both of which are integral for comprehensively representing patient history. The emergence of large language models (LLMs) has enabled the incorporation of unstructured data modalities into machine learning models that leverage EHR data. In this systematic review, we characterize studies that utilize LLM-enabled multimodal predictive modeling with EHR data. Following a screening of 641 studies, 57 met inclusion criteria. We identified three strategies for LLM-based multimodal integration: embedding, extraction, and text fusion. Delineated by the format of the unstructured data at the time of fusion, all strategies yielded performance gains (average 6.4% increase) over single modality models. LLMs facilitated modeling by generating note-embeddings for downstream prediction, extracting clinically informative variables, and summarizing long text documents prior to integration. Building on our review, we identified LLM-enhanced predictive modeling considerations that include sample size, interpretability, and computational costs. This study supports the potential value of LLMs for EHR-based predictive modeling and provides a framework for future multimodal modeling tools.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Wireless digital twins (DTs) are increasingly integrated with artificial intelligence to support online modeling, prediction, and network optimization. However, most existing approaches perform adaptation within predefined learning or optimization structures, which may become unsuitable when wireless tasks and operating conditions change. In this article, we investigate the integration of large language models (LLMs) and Bayesian optimization (BO) to extend wireless DTs from online adaptation towards algorithm-level self-evolution. We introduce an LLM-assisted BO framework in which BO provides a stable and sample-efficient optimization backbone, while the LLM determines whether selected BO components should be retained or adapted based on the current task and accumulated optimization experience. In simulations, we apply the framework to Gaussian process (GP) kernel discovery for a multi-user wireless beam-selection problem. Simulation results show that the LLM-discovered kernel improves the final BO performance by 19.7% on the training tasks compared with the strongest standard kernel baseline. The results demonstrate the potential of combining LLM flexibility with structured BO for self-evolving wireless DTs.

Medical knowledge evolves as clinical guidelines revise recommendations, yet whether large language models (LLMs) faithfully incorporate such changes remains unclear. We introduce ChronoEvo, comprising 1,709 recommendation-level revisions across 12 forms of medical knowledge change, to distinguish recognition of revised guidance from incorporation into clinical recommendations. In the primary model, 90.8% of responses recognized revisions and 80.2% were clinically correct, but only 58.5% fully incorporated guidance, yielding a 32.3-percentage-point recognition-incorporation gap. This dissociation persisted across 14 models and was corroborated by two clinicians' adjudicated assessment of 300 responses, yielding a 40.3-percentage-point gap in the validation sample. Changes in recommendation strength and patient eligibility were associated with retention of outdated guidance. A revision-salience intervention reduced outdated-content retention and improved clinical correctness but did not significantly improve full incorporation. These findings identify faithful incorporation of evolving medical knowledge as a distinct challenge for clinical LLM reliability, even when updated guideline evidence is available.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication enables connected vehicles to make safety-critical decisions, but delayed, missing, or incorrect information can compromise driving safety. Systematically testing such failures is challenging because traffic interactions, communication conditions, and application responses must be jointly configured to produce meaningful scenarios. This paper presents LAST-V2X, a language-driven, adaptive framework for automated scenario synthesis and safety testing of V2X applications. LAST-V2X leverages large language models (LLMs) to translate natural-language test descriptions into executable scenarios grounded in roadway geometry, V2X communication semantics, and vehicle behavior. The framework integrates physical traffic simulation with spatially aware communication modeling and message-level fault injection to evaluate how information degradation affects vehicle decisions. To establish whether an observed safety failure is caused by communication rather than the underlying traffic conditions, LAST-V2X employs matched executions under degraded and ground-truth information. Furthermore, an execution-guided refinement mechanism combines parameter search and LLM self-reflection to identify ineffective test configurations, improve scenario effectiveness, and produce minimal reproducible failure cases. Experiments across diverse CARLA environments and V2X safety applications demonstrate the framework's ability to generate reliable scenarios, distinguish communication-induced failures from unrelated safety violations, and substantially improve failure discovery through adaptive refinement. These results establish LAST-V2X as a systematic approach to language-driven, causally verified, and adaptive safety testing for connected vehicle systems.

The Hopfield model, originally inspired by spin glasses, occupies a central place at the intersection of statistical mechanics, neural networks, and artificial intelligence. Despite its conceptual simplicity and broad applicability, it is rarely integrated into the undergraduate physics curriculum. We present the Hopfield model as a pedagogically rich framework that naturally unifies core topics from the undergraduate physics curriculum and that provides a concise introduction based on concepts such as a model's energy function, dynamics, and pattern stability. We discuss practical aspects of its simulation and provide simulation codes. We also propose problems designed to mirror research practice, which can be included in undergraduate classes.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing project work while raising questions about how project professionals acquire and demonstrate competence. This article develops an evidence-informed framework for learning and educating project managers in AI-enabled environments. It undertakes a focused integrative analysis of findings from a 2026 survey of 300 German project professionals and selected empirical studies of AI-assisted project work, learning, and education. In the source survey, 91% reported readiness to develop competences, learning-by-doing was the most highly rated individual format, and mentoring/coaching was the highest-rated organizational support measure. Experimental and classroom evidence indicates that AI can improve task performance and provide instructional scaffolding, but output improvements do not necessarily imply durable learning or sound contextual judgment. We propose a three-part educational architecture encompassing foundational project management judgment, responsible human–AI collaboration, and project value-oriented orchestration. It is operationalized through scaffolded practice, explicit AI-use rules, progressively independent assessments, and workplace-supported development. The framework is a conceptual synthesis, not an intervention validated by the source survey. The article offers testable propositions and an evaluation agenda for universities, employers, trainers, and professional associations.

Abstract Background Artificial intelligence (AI) has achieved notable success in closed‐set classification of neurodegenerative diseases, but its performance degrades significantly in more realistic open‐set settings, such as discovering rare or novel disease subtypes from unlabeled data that are not seen during training. Purpose This study introduces, to our knowledge, the first framework for generalized category discovery (GCD) in neurodegenerative diseases using MRI. It aims to leverage labeled data from known categories to automatically identify novel categories within unlabeled datasets. Methods We propose a GCD framework integrating semi‐supervised contrastive learning with global‐local representation learning to jointly optimize feature learning. Globally, we enforce consistency between weakly augmented views of the same instance by aligning their similarity relationships with other embeddings in a support queue. Locally, we treat neighborhood embeddings from the support queue as positive pairs for cross‐instance contrastive learning, enhancing fine‐grained discrimination. This dual strategy results in a unified learning objective that is applicable to both labeled and unlabeled data, effectively narrowing the representation gap among semantically similar instances. Results We evaluate our method on a benchmark dataset comprising six neurodegenerative diseases, with over 1500 patient samples. Experimental results demonstrate that our framework consistently outperforms representative state‐of‐the‐art methods. Specifically, our method achieves 66.02% Accuracy and 60.59% Normalized Mutual Information on all categories, and 54.53% Accuracy and 16.67% Normalized Mutual Information on novel categories, surpassing existing state‐of‐the‐art methods. Conclusions Our framework underscores the model's robustness and its practical value in discovering new neurodegenerative disease conditions, highlighting its potential for advancing open‐set diagnostic AI.

Real robot data, rich across tasks and morphologies, is often treated as the bottleneck for training robot learning models, including embodied foundation models that aim for zero-shot physical transfer. In this paper, we investigate the degree to which such models can acquire necessary structure using data from systems without embodiment. To this end, we test if inexpensive, procedurally generated synthetic data can yield useful priors before a model observes any real-world behavior. We study this through robot action prediction, a natural pretraining objective and a direct test of whether structure learned from arbitrary synthetic tasks transfers to embodied settings. We introduce three data generation pipelines that model mathematical abstractions of robotic control, and use them as pretraining priors for a Transformer. We demonstrate that a model trained purely on this non-robotic data attains non-trivial zero-shot prediction performance on unseen physical robot tasks via an in-context learning mechanism, and that our specialized control priors notably improve upon generic causal priors. We also compare against a compute-matched baseline trained on real robot data, and find that it outperforms our model but only on the datasets it was trained on. These findings suggest that procedurally generated, mathematical abstractions can yield useful robotic priors, offering a potential complement to expensive embodied data collection.

Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring aims to detect potentially harmful behaviors in large language models (LLMs) from their CoTs. Intervention-based evaluations measure this property by asking whether a monitor can detect the role of an intervention from the CoT when the targeted behavior occurs, typically using minimal-criterion sensitivity ($\mathsf{TPR_{mc}}$) proposed by~\citep{guan2025monitoring}. However, a target behavior observed under intervention is not necessarily caused by it, and we show that this metric can overestimate how often a monitor detects target behaviors actually caused by the intervention. Specifically, we establish $\mathsf{TPR_{mc}}$ as an upper bound on this causal detection rate and derive a complementary lower bound, which provides a tighter evaluation framework for CoT monitorability. With this framework, we study whether LLMs can be trained to make their CoTs easier to monitor. We first construct a training dataset of paired control--intervention tasks spanning multiple intervention types. Using the dataset, we design and apply three intervention-specific training methods based on off-policy self-distillation, reinforcement learning, and on-policy self-distillation to train separate variants of each base model. Across various model-monitor configurations, all three methods generally improve CoT monitorability over the corresponding base models under our extended evaluation framework. Our code is available at https://github.com/xinyue-lxy/learning-to-be-monitored.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: This article focuses on the legal challenges arising from the use of artificial intelligence in healthcare from the perspective of global health policy. While the active application of AI at various stages of healthcare demonstrates increasing efficiency, it also increases legal risks and highlights the necessity of an adapted legal framework. The article argues that the integration of artificial intelligence in healthcare is more challenging from a legal perspective than from a technological or ethical point of view, as it actively raises issues such as patient rights, the principle of informed consent, liability, and other related concerns, requiring coherent regulatory standards and coordinated policy responses. The authors propose a human-centered governance model that ensures the best possible balance, protects human rights and minimizes legal challenges arising from AI-related outcomes.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education
